changes.text: The Channel Pump Station record said it was built in 1979, upgraded in 2010, rated 103 million gallons per day and the largest of five combined-sewer pump stations, citing the DataSF Assessor and an SF Chronicle article. Neither states any of that, and the article is about Stormwater Pump Station #6, a different building. The record now cites SF Planning's Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, chapter 7, which gives 455 Berry St, constructed 1979, upgraded 2010, 103 mgd, and continuous dry and wet weather operation. The 'largest of five' claim and the sentence about a round, tiled design were removed because no source read supports them for this station. The 1979 milestone now cites the same report.

record.notes: Channel Pump Station, 455 Berry St -- an above-grade SFPUC wastewater pump station between 6th and 7th Streets, constructed in 1979 and upgraded in 2010, with a pumping capacity of 103 million gallons per day, operating continuously in both dry and wet weather; conveys flows through the Channel force main to the Southeast Treatment Plant (source: SF Planning, Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, ch. 7 Wastewater, 2020, which describes it as operating). Identified by the owner while reviewing the tracker's remaining open plan labels -- OCII's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map marks this site 'X1' in its gray/non-developable category; this session had previously left X1 with no record after an unrelated street-cluster mislabeling. DataSF Assessor confirms blklot 3806006 as 'Industrial Gov Mixed/Other Use' at this address, with no building data on the roll. Status 'existing' (the 2020 SF Planning report above describes the station as operating; not touched by Mission Bay's redevelopment, staying as-is) per this project's own convention for pre-existing infrastructure untouched by redevelopment (e.g. UCSF's own Utilities Plant, Pier 70's Building 21).
